captions.detailed: This 3D model consists of two vertical, hollow cylindrical housings of different diameters, joined together by a central structural web. One cylinder is slightly wider and features internal stepped ledges, while the second cylinder features a full-length vertical slot along its outer wall. Two horizontal cylindrical pins/axles protrude outward from the sides of the assembly, serving as mounting points or pivots.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric dual-cylinder mounting bracket in OpenSCAD. The script should feature two parallel cylindrical housings connected by a solid bridge, with a configurable center-to-center distance parameter `dist`. Include a vertical slit on one cylinder, internal stepped bores on the other, and horizontal mounting pins extending from the sides.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using a `union()` of several `difference()` operations. The first housing is a cylinder (height 25, radius 8) hollowed out with multiple concentric cylinders to create a stepped bore. The second housing is translated by `dist` along the X-axis, consisting of a cylinder (height 25, radius 6) hollowed by a larger cylinder and cut with a thin rectangular cube to form a vertical slit. A central connecting block is made with a translated cube, which is then cleaned up by subtracting overlapping cylinders. Finally, the horizontal pins are added using rotated and translated cylinders along the Y-axis.
